QMSBR---*Quantitative Methods for Social and Behavioral Research*---is a modular collection of chapters designed to support various quantitative and statistical courses.
Its modular design serves several courses at once: each course chooses its
own route through one canonical set of chapters whose identities and links
stay stable, so a correction to a chapter improves every route that uses it.
The chapters help readers make sense of quantitative studies, following how a
study turns a question into evidence and a bounded answer. They also help
readers carry out analyses in which design, statistical reasoning,
interpretation, and reproducible computing stay connected.

**Part One** covers foundations, regression, and generalized linear models. It
moves from research questions, data, and variation through estimation, testing,
and group comparisons to computing with R and regression, and its first four
chapters can be read without running R or SPSS. **Part Two** covers factor
analysis and structural equation modeling: how observed responses represent
latent variables, and how a measurement model is developed, specified,
estimated, evaluated, and extended. **Part Three** is reserved for multilevel
and longitudinal models and is not yet available. The reading approach the
chapters share is set out on
[The Argument-Based Approach](argument-approach.qmd).

## Citation {#citation}

To cite the collection:

> Chen, J. (2026). *QMSBR: Quantitative Methods for Social and Behavioral
> Research*. <https://jinsong-chen.github.io/QMSBR/>

To cite an individual chapter, cite it by its title and give its page address,
for example:

> Chen, J. (2026). Simple linear regression (Part One, Chapter 7). In *QMSBR:
> Quantitative Methods for Social and Behavioral Research*.
> <https://jinsong-chen.github.io/QMSBR/part-one/chapter_07.html>

Also cite the original datasets, software, and studies that an analysis uses.

## Licences {#licences}

Chapter text, figures, and site prose are licensed under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Original code is
licensed under the MIT License. Simulated data created for QMSBR is dedicated
to the public domain under
[CC0 1.0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/).

Third-party items keep their own terms: the Chapter 1 student-outcome extract
from the dataset released by Realinho and colleagues (UCI Machine Learning
Repository, dataset 697; CC BY 4.0); the Chapter 2 secondary-school data
derived from the UCI Student Performance dataset (Cortez, 2008; CC BY 4.0); the
Chapter 7 extract of Galton's family heights, historical records in the public
domain transcribed by J. A. Hanley and distributed in the R package HistData;
and `apa.csl`, from the CSL styles collection (CC BY-SA 3.0). The R support
pages carry their own licence and data register. Package datasets used in
examples are loaded from their R packages and are not redistributed here.

The repository's
[LICENSE](https://github.com/Jinsong-Chen/QMSBR/blob/main/LICENSE) file is the
full statement of these terms.

## Accessibility {#accessibility}

Every chapter, part introduction, and concept reference is offered as an HTML
page and as a tagged PDF that meets the PDF/UA-2 accessibility standard. The
HTML page is the more flexible format: it provides a responsive layout,
headings, search, descriptive link text, and selectable code, and the PDF
suits printing and annotation. Figures carry alternative text, and text and
link colours are chosen for readable contrast. A navigation entry for a unit
that is not yet available is shown in a muted colour and marked as disabled,
so it is not announced or reached as a working link.

To report an accessibility barrier, open an issue in the
[repository issue tracker](https://github.com/Jinsong-Chen/QMSBR/issues) or
email [jinsong.chen@live.com](mailto:jinsong.chen@live.com), naming the page
and what got in the way.

## Using QMSBR in a course {#courses}

This site is canonical: it holds the current chapters, and courses consume it
rather than keep copies of their own. Each course chooses its own route and
sequence through the chapters. Course materials and assessment stay in the
course system, such as Moodle, and a course links to the stable chapter pages,
so its students always reach the current version of each chapter.

| This site | The course system |
|:--|:--|
| The current chapters, part introductions, and concept references | The term schedule and weekly instructions |
| Stable chapter pages and their PDFs | Announcements and deadlines |
| The chapters' own exercises | Classroom notes, assessment, feedback, and answer keys |
